{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that verbal encouragement from a superior partner would influence the participant's perception of the partner's relative ability.",
  "design": "mixed, 3 (condition: individual control, partner with-encouragement, partner-without-encouragement) x 2 (performance block) factorial design",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Participants were assigned to either an individual control condition or one of two partner conditions where they were led to believe they were the 'weak link' on a team with a superior partner. In the encouragement condition, participants received prerecorded verbal encouragement from the partner.",
  "outcome_measure": "Participant's rating of their partner's relative ability on a 9-point scale (1 = 'I am much more capable' to 9 = 'my partner is much more capable').",
  "population_and_setting": "College students recruited from introductory psychology and kinesiology courses at a large Midwestern university, tested in a laboratory setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 115,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via introductory psychology and kinesiology courses; participants received course credit.",
  "analysis_plan": "A 2 (encouragement vs no-encouragement) x 2 (sex) ANOVA on partner relative ability ratings.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "The study used a confederate to simulate a partner via a prerecorded video link. Participants were led to believe they were the 'weak link' by providing them with bogus feedback that the partner performed 1.4 times better than the participant."
}
